prompt:
A hand-painted map of a whole continent seen from directly above, in the manner of a painted fantasy map such as a map of Middle-earth: coastlines, mountain ranges drawn as shaded ridges, rivers as fine dark lines running downhill to the sea, forests as textured masses, marsh, desert and open plain each in its own tone. Oil on parchment in a 19th-century academic manner with a smooth, finely blended surface, soft glazed transitions, fine detail, no heavy impasto. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and sea-green with near-black shading. Less detail at larger scale; nothing drawn smaller than a hill or a wood; no settlements, no roads, no figures, no borders between countries. No text, no lettering, no compass rose, no scale bar, no frame, no grid, not photographic. The whole sheet is land and sea; nothing is cut off at the edges.

One large landmass fills a square sheet, north at the top, with sea-green sea on all four sides in a band about a twelfth of the sheet wide, so that the whole coast is inside the sheet. The land is broad everywhere, roughly as wide as it is tall, with an irregular coast and no long peninsulas. In the exact middle of the land lies one great round lake of dark still water, about a twelfth of the sheet across, in a wide shallow basin of pale meadow ringed at a distance by low worn hills. One wide river leaves the lake on its west side and runs west across low rolling hills and open plain to the western sea. Along the north coast, in its middle third, runs a belt of pale snow-covered high ground, cut by four or five long narrow valleys that run north to a grey sea; the coast there is notched with narrow inlets, and one small lake lies in the longest valley. The north-east quarter is filled by the highest mountains of the land, a broad broken range with snow on its peaks and notched passes, running from the snow country south-east toward the east coast; inside the range lies one broad green valley, cupped and ringed entirely by peaks, and short rivers run from the range south-west down to the central lake. South of the range, rough dry ochre hills. In the middle of the eastern side stands one great dark forest; along the forest's southern edge lies a wide belt of dark green fen and reed, with a slow river sliding through the fen eastward to the east coast, and low hills south of the fen. Between the forest and the east coast, a small country of steep wooded hills. In the south-east, many braided threads of river run south-east through pale misty lowland with wooded banks to the south-east coast. South of the central basin lies a high open brown heath. From it one long river runs due south: braided in its middle course, then slow and wide through wet green meadows, ending in a broad dark marsh delta on the south coast. East of the delta, pale salt flats lie along the coast. In the south-west, a broad green and gold river valley runs from the heath south-west to the sea, between two long lines of brown heather upland, with dark woods in its side valleys. In the north-west, two wide slow rivers wander through flat pale green lowland to the north-west coast, with low hills along the edges of that lowland. Between the north-west lowland and the western river lies a wide open plain of pale gold grass. Elsewhere between these countries, open grass and brown moor. Light falls evenly; the sea darkens toward the edges of the sheet.
